Prerequisites

In this game, we pair each number with the name of its family, using the second column of Table 1 of the text Naming. To make the most of this activity, we recommend reviewing first:

  • Naming: in this text, Table 1 presents the names of the families, from Quintillion down to Units and from Tenths down to Trillionths ().
  • Sequence game (Orders): the game whose mechanics this one follows, pairing numbers with the names of their orders ().

Rules

The goal of the game is to pair each number with the name of its family, following the second column of Table 1 of Naming: Quintillion, Quadrillion, Trillion, Billion, Million, Thousand, Units, Tenths, Hundredths, Thousandths, Millionths, Billionths and Trillionths. The family of a number is the range of values it lies in: 4,000,000 lies in the Million family and 0.004 in the Thousandths family. In each round, six numbers appear on the left, each one belonging to a different family, and the names of these same six families appear on the right in a different order. Select a number and then select the name of its family; if the pair is correct, both buttons are highlighted and stay in place. If the pair is wrong, a hint appears telling you which family the number belongs to, or which values the family you chose contains, so you can learn from the mistake and try again.

The game has three levels. In the first level, six numbers are drawn at random from the seven families of whole numbers, from Quintillion down to Units. In the second level, three of the drawn numbers are whole numbers and three are decimals between zero and one, mixing whole-number families such as Million with decimal families such as Hundredths. In the third level, all six numbers are decimals between zero and one: one is drawn from each of the six families from Tenths down to Trillionths.

When you match all six pairs of a level, a congratulatory message is displayed and the button Next level becomes available. After you finish the third level, a final congratulatory message is displayed. You can start a new round at any time by clicking the button New Game.

Sequence games (Decimal order)

Connect each number on the left with the name of its family on the right. Select a number, then select the name of its family to form the pair. Before choosing the family, ask yourself whether the number is a whole number or a decimal: whole numbers belong to the families from Units up to Quintillion, while decimals between zero and one belong to the families from Tenths down to Trillionths. To find the family quickly, group the digits of a whole number in threes from the right (one group means Units, two mean Thousand, three mean Million, four mean Billion, five mean Trillion, six mean Quadrillion, seven mean Quintillion) or count the digits after the decimal point (one means Tenths, two mean Hundredths, three mean Thousandths, six mean Millionths, nine mean Billionths, twelve mean Trillionths).

PERFECT! You matched all the numbers with the names of their families!
